# Max Keiser Puzzle Investigation Log

## Baseline

- Source article: `magazine.pdf` / `keyser bitcoin .pdf`, article pages 75-80.
- Public clue found externally: Max described the target as a private Bitcoin key encoded in the Bitcoin Magazine piece, and gave "Mirror writing: neurological reflections on an unusual phenomenon" as a clue.
- Source audit:
  - ThreadReader archive for tweet `1632068898169450497` confirms the public announcement text: Max said he hid a private Bitcoin key encoded in the piece he wrote for `@BitcoinMagazine`, "Nobody's figured it out yet," and "it's for 20 BTC."
  - The archived announcement page says the thread had 6 tweets, but only the first text is recoverable from ThreadReader; several content slots are blank.
  - Twitter oEmbed still returns the original announcement tweet text and date: March 4, 2023.
  - The attached tweet image was recovered from `https://pbs.twimg.com/media/FqZGAb7aYAEdnKL.jpg`; it shows Max holding the Bitcoin Magazine El Salvador issue open to the "OVERDOSE" feature.
  - Twitter oEmbed also recovers clue tweet `1632391507008278528` from March 5, 2023: it quotes the exact title `"Mirror writing: neurological reflections on an unusual phenomenon"` and contains two shortened links.
    - `https://t.co/WkSDXKwSiv` expands to `https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC2117809/`.
    - `https://t.co/3NrEhxV2Iz` expands back to the original announcement tweet `https://twitter.com/maxkeiser/status/1632068898169450497`.
  - Bitcointalk topic `5450165.0` independently quotes the announcement and the clue, links the clue tweet as `https://twitter.com/maxkeiser/status/1632391507008278528?s=20`, identifies the source as Bitcoin Magazine's Salvador Issue, and links the Google Drive article PDF.
  - Bitcointalk page 2 does not add a credible clue. It mainly reinforces that no funding address/public key was posted, so any solver must guard against accidental active-address false positives.
  - Bitcoin Magazine's store page for "The El Salvador Issue, #24" says the issue is the first relaunch edition and is "Featuring OVERDOSE with Max Keiser."
  - The mirror-writing clue is the exact title of G. D. Schott's 2007 paper, "Mirror writing: neurological reflections on an unusual phenomenon" (PMID `16963501`, PMCID `PMC2117809`, DOI `10.1136/jnnp.2006.094870`).
  - The paper defines mirror writing as writing in the opposite direction with individual letters reversed, most easily read with a mirror. It repeatedly emphasizes left-hand writing, reversed order/form, bimanual mirror movements, the corpus callosum, the right hemisphere, and Leonardo da Vinci.
- Existing local solver over-reported BIP39 hits because `src/data/wordlist.js` had 2051 words instead of the official 2048-word BIP39 English list. This is fixed by loading `bip39/src/wordlists/english.json`.

## Active Hypotheses

- H1: The answer is not a seed phrase; it is a private key, likely encoded visually by mirror/fold mechanics.
- H2: The colored/inverted highlights are selection masks, not final words by themselves.
- H3: The "mirror writing" clue may imply folding/reflection of page pairs 75/79 and 76/78, extracting overlap/intersections/differences.
- H4: Bold words and highlighted letters may provide indices/order rather than direct seed material.
- H5: The clue may refer to the "OVERDOSE" column/feature mechanics, not only the local article pages. The recovered tweet image and official store copy both foreground "OVERDOSE," while later Max columns include mirror-themed titles.

## Visual Workstream

- Build masks for orange highlights and inverted black/white highlight blocks.
- Extract connected components and bounding boxes per page.
- Compare page-pair reflections:
  - 75 vs 79
  - 76 vs 78
  - possibly 75 vs 78 and 76 vs 79, based on magazine fold/spread geometry.
- Test overlap, XOR, and bounding-box center mappings onto article text.

## Current Assessment

- The reflected-highlight-mask mechanism is real and produces intentional-looking text selections, but direct use as a brainwallet/private key has no activity.
- The high-resolution source scan confirms the same reflected-highlight mechanism and closes the earlier bad page-78 mapping branch as an artifact.
- The second-stage encoding pass over reflected selections has no activity after filtering low-entropy false positives, including the full per-box expansion across standard address types.
- Exact fold calibration improved the readability of reflected selections but did not produce visible WIF/hex/seed-like page-77 index outputs, and the calibrated page-77 legacy-address check found no activity.
- Remaining possible work is the low-signal exhaustive space: raw base58 sliding windows, raw ASCII/word-position windows, more precise/manual mask calibration, and non-standard address/key derivations. These spaces are much larger and produce many accidental hits unless aggressively filtered.

  - `scripts/highres_reflection_extract.py` was fixed to rebuild its high-resolution source images from `magazine.pdf` under `analysis_outputs/source_images/`, instead of relying on deleted `/tmp/magazine_highres-*.jpg` files.
  - `scripts/source_alignment_audit.py` now compares high-res magazine images against OCR-PDF images, writes `analysis_outputs/source_audit/source_alignment_audit.md`, and generates high-res mirrored overlay/diff images.

    - `magazine.pdf`: 2544x3264, 300 ppi, page rotation 180.
    - `keyser bitcoin .pdf`: 2040x2805, 255 ppi, PDF24 OCR layer, no page rotation.

    5. If that still fails, the next external dependency is a physical magazine scan/photo, because the current digital sources disagree enough that precise fold geometry may be off.
